validator: draft 1 passes validate.mjs with no hard or soft problems; the faults below are the critic's.
keep: The idea is named up front in one sentence: a straight-line part minus a squared part, an upside-down U, zero where the parts are equal and highest halfway between those roots.

Each job's squared part is given its cause, not asserted: two things that both grow with the input multiplied together (falling speed and time; current and the volts lost inside; the load on the left and its lever arm).

The brief's figures are used throughout and agree with the cited rules: 19.6t − 4.9t² lands at 4 s and peaks at 19.6 m at 2 s [1][3]; 12I − 0.5I² is zero at 0 A and 24 A = E ÷ r [4], peaks at 12 A, 72 W, with the load at 0.5 Ω = r [5]; 6x − x² is zero at the supports [6] and peaks at 9 kN·m = wL²/8 at midspan [7].

Every lesson-7 misconception in the brief has a DO screen with its own wrong pick: keeping the impossible root (screen 4, the deck ball's −1 s [14]), P against R (screen 8, 64 W not 144 W), most power taken as best efficiency (screen 7's split bar and practice), plus leaving out the squared part (10, 12, 13) and the peak halfway between start and end when they are at different heights (11).
Thirteen screens alternate SHOW (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) and DO (2, 4, 6, 8, 10) and end on three mixed puzzles, one per job (11-13).
Practice has the safe way first, steps, two rules of thumb, a worked beam example checked against wL²/8, and the mistakes.
fix: Causal step skipped (why 4.9t²): 'In Calculus fundamentals a speed that grows steadily added up to ½ × 9.8 × t²' leans on a back-reference. Give the step in words: gravity adds 9.8 m/s of downward speed every second, so over t seconds the average downward speed is halfway from 0 to 9.8t, which is 4.9t, and 4.9t for t seconds is 4.9t².
Course puzzle left unanswered in words: say why the best current is exactly half the short-circuit current, because the peak sits halfway between the roots 0 and E ÷ r.

Unreadable label: E is used in the explanation (EI, E ÷ r) without being named there, and w and L in wL²/8 are never named. Name E as the battery's voltage with nothing connected, and w and L as the load on each metre and the span.
Unexplained unit: kN·m. Say a moment is measured in newton metres, the unit a torque setting uses, here in kilonewton metres.
False absolute: 'where a bending moment must be zero' holds for simply supported ends, which is what the source says. Say the beam rests on two simple supports that let it turn.
False absolute in the takeaway: an upside-down U from a line minus a square has roots only when the two parts meet. Add 'when it has them'.

Overstated closing: 'real curves come out a little different' is not true for every ball (a light, fast one is slowed a lot by the air). Say they differ most where those effects are large, and point to Trigonometry for a throw at an angle.

Value word dressed as fact: 'not its best use' (analogy breaks) and 'Taking the most power as the best use' (practice). Say what is true: at the peak half the power the battery makes heats the battery, so the most power to the load is not the most efficient.
Paragraph 2 carries three jobs and paragraph 3 mixes the peak with the cautions. Split so the roots and peaks have their own paragraph and the cautions close with the takeaway (four paragraphs).
Term used once only: maximum power transfer must be used again; use it in the rule of thumb.
